items.title: feat(id): add journaled scheduled events for worlds
items.body:
## Summary
- Worlds can schedule host events durably: `schedule.at` (fire a program event at a unix-ms time) and `schedule.cancel`. Both are ordinary grants on the existing ledger.
- Fired events go only to the program as host events (`{"cap":"schedule","event":"fired","id":…}`). Joiners never see them.
- Pending schedules survive restart through the journal and the checkpoint. A schedule that was due while the server was down fires on the first wakeup with `"late":true`.
- Bounds: 64 pending per world, ids of 1 to 64 printable ASCII bytes (spaces allowed), at most 30 days ahead, no duplicate pending id.

Design record: `doc/2026-10-17T10-00-00Z_feature_scheduled_events/`. Stacked on #234.

## Deviations from the brief, decided in the work
- **Fire order is accept → journal the delivery → journal `ScheduleFired`.** The brief said "journaled before delivery". The existing input path runs `update` before it journals, and journaling first would record a delivery the program refused. The trade-off: a crash between the two appends can deliver a fire again after restart. The repeat carries `late:true`, and replays still match the journal.
- **Tick deadlines use the minimum over armed ticks.** The old code read the first interval's deadline, which is not always the earliest. This is a behaviour change for ticks, found while adding schedule wakeups.
- **Pending schedules survive `InstallProgram`**, because they are world state.
- **The wire carries only `bad_args`** for refused schedule requests. `CapError` has no message field, so the reason goes to the core error and a debug log.

## Rollback (corrected)
A binary built before this change reads an unknown entry as a torn append when the entry is the last line, and truncates it. That silently drops the newest schedule or ceiling change. Only a non-final unknown entry makes the older binary refuse the journal. Restore a pre-change journal backup before rolling back. A separate journal fix is in progress so that future binaries fail loudly on this case.

## Validation
- `cargo test --lib --no-default-features --features sandbox,world schedule`: 17 passed (16 schedule tests and the Roc request-builder test), repeated 3 times.
- `cargo test --lib` (default features): 1347 passed, 4 ignored (pre-existing).
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean. Clippy via the rustup 1.97.0 cargo exits 0; plain `cargo clippy` fails with E0514 as before.
- Not verified: a real pre-change binary; fault injection between the two journal appends; timing under load (tests use sleeps and 3-second deadlines); a compiled Roc program that fires a schedule end to end.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added one-time scheduled events that can be created and cancelled. Events are delivered to the program when due, including while a durable world is disconnected.
  * Schedules persist across program installs and restarts. Events that fire after their scheduled time are marked as late.
  * Scheduling is limited to 64 pending events per world, with printable IDs up to 64 characters and a maximum 30-day scheduling horizon. Past times are allowed.
  * Schedule requests require the appropriate capability permissions.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.body:
## Drew's direct order (2026-11-10, pool-intelligence chat) — TOP PRIORITY

"make _openai that does it all without codex" — supersedes the prove-the-Codex-sync mandate for the openai.main door.

## Problem

The openai.main door's credential is fed by the Muse: `codex-sync.ts` copies `~/.codex/auth.json` into the store and stamps the credential `externalRefresh`, so the provider itself never refreshes it. When the sync path broke, the door auth-died for ~a day (0/9,897 Authentication on 2026-11-10's pool-intelligence window) while quota reads called it healthy. openai.alternate already proves the self-renewing pattern: its own in-store OAuth credential (chatgpt-headless), refreshed in-process, no Codex involvement (#8102 self-renewal audit).

## Build

A self-contained `_openai` provider door for the drewrypope ChatGPT account:

- Own credential in the OpenCode credential store under its own integration id, obtained via the fork's existing OpenAI OAuth flows (seeded from the currently-valid drewrypope tokens if that avoids a fresh consent; the seeded row must NOT carry the externalRefresh stamp).
- Own refresh token, refreshed in-process by the provider (Integration connection resolve), exactly like openai.alternate. No reading `~/.codex/auth.json`, no codex-sync in its path, no Muse involvement at any point.
- Direct HTTPS plan auth to the ChatGPT backend in-process (native openai provider wire), no proxy hop.
- The Codex sync must never write this door's credential (explicit guard + test in the fork).
- Config: seat `_openai` as the main door in `openai-plan` (replacing openai.main's seat; openai.alternate untouched). Keep the openai.main definition until `_openai` is proven, then retire the Codex-sync dependency for the main door.

## Proof standard (traffic, never a quota read alone)

- route_attempt rows under the `_openai` provider id: successes, or — while the weekly quota wall lasts (reset Fri Nov 13 08:28 CST) — attempts that pass auth and fail only QuotaExceeded.
- A successful in-process token refresh cycle in the provider's own store with `~/.codex/auth.json` untouched/unread.
- Negative proof: the door still works with the Codex sync path disabled for it.

Refs: #7991 (closed, the auth-death incident), #5705 (Luna re-lead off openai.main), #8102 (self-renewal audit). Fork: developing-today-forks/opencode.

## Problem

The repo-health OpenChamber queue worker cannot claim any task: the queue lane registry rejects its registered lane id.

Verified 2026-11-07 ~08:07Z by the event-hook worker (`repo-worker-openchamber`, generation 1912):

- `fleet queue health` (laptop binary) succeeds and reports the Turso store (`fleet-queue-dezren39.aws-us-east-1.turso.io`): `repo-health-openchamber-pilot` = 32 queued, 0 claimed, 5 parked, 11 blocked.
- `fleet queue list --queue repo-health-openchamber-pilot` succeeds.
- `fleet queue claim --queue repo-health-openchamber-pilot --worker repo-worker-openchamber --lane openchamber-a --lease-seconds 2700` returns: `claim_repo_task: unknown lane_id openchamber-a` (broker exit 4).

`openchamber-a` is the lane id pinned in the worker runbook (same registered id the scheduled Lane A shift uses; the bare `A` form was rejected in the 2026-11-03 incident, and #4780 covered scheduled-lane UUIDs being rejected — this is the named lane on the current store).

## Impact

Per the runbook §1/§0b, a lane-id rejection from a healthy backend is a verdict, not a backend failure: the worker stops and reports rather than retrying or switching to GitHub fallback. All 32 queued OpenChamber tasks are unclaimable by this worker until the registry is fixed.

## Fix needed

Register/restore lane `openchamber-a` (worker `repo-worker-openchamber`, queue `repo-health-openchamber-pilot`) in the lane registry backing the Turso queue store, or publish the replacement lane id and update `repo-queue-worker-instruction-openchamber.md` to match. Verify with a live claim by the hook worker.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fleet queue claim --queue repo-health-openchamber-pilot --worker repo-worker-openchamber --lane openchamber-a` (and the code/opencode/nix lane equivalents) succeeds against the Turso store, or the lane registry is corrected so the pinned lane ids in the runbooks are the registered ones
- [ ] A claim rejected for lane reasons is distinguishable in logs from a backend outage (verdict vs failure) without reading broker internals

# DST-04 — Extend existing Projector webhook intake as authenticated bounded transport/dedup, then fan out a typed field-scoped operation through the existing Fleet authority adapter

<!-- pmo-9196:DST-04 -->

**Issue title:** `design(pm-orchestration): Extend existing Projector webhook intake as authenticated bounded transport/dedup, then fan out a typed field-scoped operation through the existing Fleet authority adapter`  
**Design parent:** #9200 · **Scope:** #9200 priority distribution · **Version:** V3 proposal; not an authorization to implement. **Requirement IDs (ALLOCATED):** C-R005, C-R009, C-R066, C-R068, C-R077, C-R079, C-R107, C-R108, H-R005, H-R012, H-R017, H-R024, H-R031, O-R018, O-R023, P-R009. **Slice status:** curated implementation/research slice. **Pinned baseline:** `a038f084dbeb525494d7bb928ad91f597db2ac51`.

This batch creates design/research/validation handoff issues only. After PR #9225 is merged and this slice's granular prerequisites are resolved, a separately scoped implementation issue may be filed; production adoption, migration, deployment, and live acceptance remain separately authorized stages. The local FDR decisions are accepted design defaults; global #9180 registration is pending and is not a blocker to this bounded design work.

## Goal and deliverable

Map already-authenticated, delivery-deduplicated priority label/removal events into the shared Fleet command contract and reconcile echoes without granting the disposable projector authority. Reuse existing HMAC intake/hot ledger; add no policy or remote mutation to webhook.ts.

Deliver this bounded slice only. It enables downstream work only after its stated contracts and prerequisites are accepted; it does not imply that other component specs, closed parent issues, source code, tests, deployments, or runtime behavior are complete.

## Existing V1 event/projector substrate to consume

At pinned source, `pm-stack/projector/src/webhook.ts:7-57` already verifies bounded raw-body HMAC-SHA256 and `pm-stack/projector/README.md:23-30,145-179` documents supported events, `event_id=delivery:subevent`, `pmp_hot_events`, per-consumer high-water cursors and monotone durable sweep acknowledgements. This is a disposable projection ledger, not canonical Fleet command acceptance or a writeback authority (`README.md:3-8`). Consume it as a verified-input/projection-fanout seam only where the current owner supports it. Add no HMAC/auth service, no priority policy or remote mutation in `webhook.ts`, no Project writer, and no loop treating a Fleet projection echo as human intent. This slice owns label-event-to-shared-command mapping and tests for actor/capability authorization at the authoritative consumer; delivery-ID dedupe remains distinct from operation idempotency.

**Ownership resolution:** the source appendix's `webhook.ts` file suggestion is superseded by this V1 census overlay: do not put priority policy, command authorization, or remote writes in the HMAC helper. Existing HMAC remains read/auth intake only; Fleet's typed operation owner handles authorization/effects.
## Owned files and boundaries

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/distribution.rs`
- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/contracts.rs`
- `pm-stack/projector/test/priority-webhook.test.ts`

Explicit read-only consumers (not writable ownership): pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/contracts.rs, pm-stack/projector/src/webhook.ts.

Use the existing Fleet queue/PM Stack/adapter owners named in the design; do not add a queue, database, scheduler, service, resolver, executable, GitHub client, or general creation-outbox producer. Shared CLI glue remains owned by the single CLI-13 registration slice. Do not edit #6533 or duplicate its live acceptance; consume #9028/#9073–#9076/#9079/#9081/#9178/#9179/#3424/#8575/#8579 as applicable, not as replacement work.

## Prerequisites and sequencing

Hard blockers named by the source slice, after granular-key normalization: AUTH-01, DST-01, DST-03, DSP-01
File-collision sequencing edges added by stable topological serialization: none.
Existing issue references retained as non-blocking runtime/evidence gates: none.
Domain-starter parent references are never emitted as hard native blockers. Source parents normalized to granular slices or runtime gates: #9208→AUTH-01.

Source-local candidate aliases normalized for this packet: DST-CMD-01 → DST-01, CLI-02; DST-INTENT-01 → REL-03; AUTH-OP-01 → AUTH-01.


Use only granular issue-key edges after all keys are resolved. Never make a whole domain starter a hard blocker when it creates a cycle. File collisions are hard sequencing edges. Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `pmo_distribution_priority_webhook_maps_to_shared_command; pmo_distribution_protected_expedite_label_event_is_denied`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_priority_webhook_maps_to_shared_command (verify exact test name with -- --list first). Also verify `pmo_distribution_protected_expedite_label_event_is_denied` is listed, then run `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_protected_expedite_label_event_is_denied`.`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

Extend existing Projector webhook intake as authenticated bounded transport/dedup, then fan out a typed field-scoped operation through the existing Fleet authority adapter; no new service. Reuse `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts` route, `src/webhook.ts` HMAC/bounded-body helper, delivery ledger and hot-cursor protocol; test at `pm-stack/projector/test/priority-webhook.test.ts` plus Fleet authority module.

Negative coverage: stale input, duplicate/replay, ambiguous resource, unauthorized actor, partial remote effect, unknown version, and no false verified/completed result where applicable.

### Existing Drew-only protected-expedite gate (#7030; no re-ratification)

Consume the existing #7030 protected expedite membership/value and the dated `pm-stack/design-reprioritization-2026-11-12.md` record. Protection is an owner-policy write restriction, not a new urgency score, hold, or execution bypass. Re-read the versioned `fleet.owner-priority-policy/v1` policy and protected membership under the same atomic work-version check; `owner_policy_ref` is a meaningful intent precondition. Only the currently authenticated configured Drew owner action may change protected membership, intrinsic value, peer placement or priority-label intent. Routine manual edits, automation/aging/clump/hysteresis, label normalization/removal, mobile actions and slash commands must return `OWNER_POLICY_PROTECTED` with no change; stale policy ref returns `OWNER_POLICY_VERSION_CONFLICT`; missing/unverifiable policy fails closed for affected mutations. Removing a mirror label does not unprotect an item. Reads and otherwise eligible execution are not globally blocked. Preserve #7030's exact `expedite=15` / `next-up=25` values; do not reratify or translate urgency 450/Do Now into queue priority.

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: Additive and reversible only after existing owner/schema review; retain prior data and behavior; no silent fallback or dual authority.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

## Source trail

- Raw source refs: handoff `sources/01_handoff_pm_stack_fleet_orchestration.md`; charter `sources/02_charter_v1_1.md`; recovered original `sources/04_recovered_original_combined_design.md`; cited source section(s) in `sources/03_full_orchestration_proposal.md` as named by the component; exact occurrence citations are in the curated trace above when allocated.
- Design ref: `components/9200-priority-distribution.md`, slice `DST-04` (proposal only).
- Prior-art/evidence receipts: `research/track-a-state-of-art.md`, `research/track-b-state-of-art.md`, `research/track-b-sources.json`; additional exact evidence anchors for this slice: pm-stack/projector/src/webhook.ts:7-57, pm-stack/projector/README.md:3-8,23-30,145-179, pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts:25-52, https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/7030#issuecomment-6715673367, pm-stack/design-reprioritization-2026-11-12.md:11-15,22,122,207, architecture.md#protected-owner-priority-policy.
- Parent-approved support mapping (validation/expansion support only, not a direct slice-key match): none.
- Existing external requirement refs not assigned a new curated ID: none.
- Command allocation: `flag.remove, metadata.labels`. Full command inventory remains `census/commands.jsonl`; exact allocation source is `census/command-slice-map.jsonl` (215 rows, no wildcard). V1 baseline keys are not refiled as duplicate implementation issues.
- Shared architecture: `architecture.md`; FDR index: `decisions/README.md` (all FDR-PMO records remain proposed, not ratified).

---

### Original slice text (preserved)

| `DST-04` / recommended | Extend existing Projector webhook intake as authenticated bounded transport/dedup, then fan out a typed field-scoped operation through the existing Fleet authority adapter; no new service. Reuse `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts` route, `src/webhook.ts` HMAC/bounded-body helper, delivery ledger and hot-cursor protocol; test at `pm-stack/projector/test/priority-webhook.test.ts` plus Fleet authority module. | `DST-CMD-01`; granular `AUTH-OP-01` from #9208; `DST-INTENT-01`; existing Fleet command adapter contract. Projector deployment liveness remains unverified. | Delivery GUID dedup is distinct from Fleet operation idempotency; Projector store remains disposable/non-authoritative; authenticated principal/capability is checked by Fleet authority; no projector GH/Project mutation; unauthorized/conflicting label cannot mutate canonical state; final-label removal preserves score and requests triage. |
**Future red-first test commands / oracles per issue:** Exact future Rust test commands are: DST-01 `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_command_identity_reason_and_version`; DST-03 `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_atomic_intent_revision`; DST-05 `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_projection_replay`; DST-06 `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_host_order_hash`; DST-07 `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml -p fleet-queue --lib --features client,queue-broker pmo_distribution_unknown_version_degrades`. Before each, run that exact command with `-- --list` and assert the named test exists; zero-test success is not acceptance. DST-01 oracle enumerates each reason code and checks field-effect class/no mutation on rejection or unsupported code. DST-02: `cd pm-stack/dispatch && bun test test/validate.test.ts` proves 15/25 round-trip exactly, not current snapping. DST-04 first asserts `test -f pm-stack/projector/test/priority-webhook.test.ts`, then runs `cd pm-stack/projector && bun test test/priority-webhook.test.ts`; DST-05 likewise asserts `test -f pm-stack/projector/test/priority-reconcile.test.ts` before `cd pm-stack/projector && bun test test/priority-reconcile.test.ts`. Both projector oracles cover replay, stale revision, partial effects and readback repair. These are future red-first specs, not current tests. No test may trust `actor_ref` or client-supplied authorization. Hard blockers are granular keys above; #9079/#9081 hosted and #9201 mobile are soft consumers.

items.body:
**Design scope only — no data moves in this issue's first pass.**

## What moves
- From: Supabase (`muse-dev2`) `ci.events` (10,952 live rows, 31.8 MB — ~2.9 KB/row of jsonb webhook payload)
- To: Turso, staging tier, partitioned by day/repo

## Why
A pure append-only CI webhook ledger: 10,957 inserts / 0 updates in the stats window since 2026-10-29, no foreign keys, read by scan (its one view, `ci.recent_failures`, is a filtered scan). It is the fastest-growing table in the project by bytes and has no transactional consumer — under the §9 placement rule it is a Turso stream, not Postgres state.

Design doc: §9 of `doc/2026-11-04T21-27-34Z_design_atlas_scaler_revision/` (PR #5667, addendum PR #5689).

## Risks
- The webhook receiver is a live write path — cutover must not drop events during deploys (receiver-side buffering or dual-write).
- `recent_failures` consumers (alerting? dashboards?) must be inventoried first; failure-visibility must not regress during the move.
- Retention is currently unbounded; the Turso design should state a retention window rather than replicating unbounded growth.

## Sketch of steps
1. Inventory the receiver(s) and every reader of `ci.events` / `ci.recent_failures`.
2. Design the Turso table + a `recent_failures`-equivalent query; set retention (propose 90 days hot, cold export beyond).
3. Dual-write at the receiver, backfill the retention window, diff failure queries.
4. Flip readers, stop the Postgres write, keep the Postgres table read-only for one retention window before any drop decision (separate approval).

Links: design doc PR #5667 · addendum PR #5689 · tracking dezren39/hatch-personal#21

items.title: Provider browser-auth auto-renewal — standing-rule follow-through (OpenDesign keeper landed; Meta / Mistral / Claude / ClinePass gaps)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: effort/l

labels.name: meta/enriched

items.body:
Drew's standing rule (2026-11-05 01:10 CST): no provider integration may depend on a browser cookie/session that silently expires. Every browser-dependent auth must have (a) an auto-renewing long-lived token, or (b) built-in cookie auto-renewal (automatic re-capture/refresh, e.g. via CDP against the standing signed-in laptop Helium profile, on cadence and on auth failure), with an alert BEFORE hard expiry when renewal fails. Manual re-import steps and one-shot fix-it crons are not an end state.

LANDED with this issue's opening pass:
- OpenDesign session keeper in the quota gatherer (pm-stack aggregator src/opendesign-renewal.ts): per-tick session read (the Better Auth session slides — verified live 2026-11-05: expiresAt = read-time + 7 days), horizon recorded in ~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/opendesign-renewal.json, CDP re-capture from the laptop Helium with validate-before-store when the stored session fails or runs low, and an alert state while days remain when renewal cannot complete. The one-shot opendesign-cookie-reimport-nov5 cron is retired once the keeper verified live.

REMAINING GAPS (each is follow-through under the rule, not a new decision):
1. Meta portal fetcher (#6079): the auto-renewal requirement is recorded on that issue (comment 6652154440) — the restore must ship with CDP cookie re-capture + pre-expiry alert built in, not a manual capture step.
2. Mistral console credits leg (openchamber#1630): /api/billing/credits is cookie-only (both API keys 401). If the usage producer lands on that leg, it needs the same CDP re-capture pattern as the OpenDesign keeper. The plan leg (whoami / account-context) is key-authed and needs no browser.
3. OpenDesign browser re-arm: the laptop Helium profile currently holds NO Open Design session (verified 2026-11-05 — the profile cookie DB has no open-design rows; the Oct 29 import's session lived in a profile state that did not survive). The keeper's capture leg therefore cannot renew from the browser until someone signs into Open Design in that profile once (Google SSO click-through — proven agent-doable 2026-10-29, no Drew-only step hit then). Until re-armed, renewal-by-use (sliding session, ~7d horizon, checked every 15-min tick) is the live mechanism and the keeper alerts with days of lead if it degrades.
4. Claude Code leaf credential: ~/.claude/.credentials.json holds an OAuth pair whose refreshTokenExpiresAt is 2026-11-09T06:27Z. Renewal is the CLI's built-in refresh — automatic when the CLI runs — but the claude-code provider is disabled in config, so nothing runs it; if the refresh token lapses, re-login is Drew-only (interactive OAuth). Surface before 2026-11-09 if the provider is to be re-enabled. Side observation: the gatherer's recorded credentialExpiresAt for claude (2026-11-05T14:31:57Z) reads +8h against the file's expiresAt (06:31:57Z, same minutes/seconds/ms) — check the lib's normalizeTimestamp for an offset bug before relying on it for alert lead times.
5. ClinePass native adapter (dormant — CLINEPASS_CREDENTIAL_REF unset on the laptop gatherer unit): its dashboard token is session-class by design (401/403 = session-expired + needsRelogin in src/clinepass-adapter.ts). Do not enable it without a renewal story. The live module read uses the ClinePass API key and is unaffected.
6. Alert surfacing: the OpenDesign keeper's alert today is its state file + the gatherer journal. Surface renewal alerts (opendesign-renewal.json status=attention, and equivalents as other providers gain keepers) on the aggregator board / morning readout so a failing renewal is seen without reading state files.

Full inventory: provider-quota-registry.md (auth inventory section, 2026-11-05) and ~/memory/topics/provider-auth-renewal-2026-11-05.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Meta portal fetcher (#6079) ships with CDP cookie re-capture + pre-expiry alert built in — no manual capture step.
- [ ] The Mistral console credits leg (openchamber#1630), if used, has the same CDP re-capture pattern; the key-authed plan leg needs no browser path.
- [ ] The OpenDesign browser re-arm gap is closed: the laptop Helium profile holds a live Open Design session the keeper can slide/renew, or the keeper's alert fires before hard expiry.
- [ ] Every browser-dependent provider auth in the fleet has (a) an auto-renewing long-lived token or (b) built-in cookie auto-renewal with a pre-expiry alert — an inventory on this issue proves none is left on manual re-import.

items.title: Move opencode executions to laptop-side scheduled tasks — retire the Muse boot handoff

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

items.body:
**Decision (Drew, 2026-10-31):** tasks assigned the **opencode execution lane** must be triggered by scheduled tasks on the laptop/OpenChamber side. No Muse cron boots, launches, or hands off to OpenCode. Muse lanes keep claiming and assigning; execution starts without Muse in the loop.

**Why:** execution already spends only provider-plan quotas, but the triggers and supervision are Muse cron jobs — in the Oct 30 check-in window the conductor burned 96M input and its still-running predecessors (openchamber-dispatcher + openchamber-babysitter) ~199M more, i.e. Muse tokens spent just to start and watch work that runs entirely elsewhere.

**Mechanism — OpenChamber scheduled tasks (corrected 2026-10-31, Drew):** OpenChamber **does** have native scheduled tasks, and they are the mechanism for this change: the schedule lives on the OpenChamber side, not in Muse cron and not in OS timers. OpenCode itself lacks the capability — the #2019 investigation (comment 6494101941) audited OpenCode core and the fleet fork and correctly found no scheduler there (upstream request anomalyco/opencode#41906 open), but it did not audit OpenChamber's own feature set; its systemd-timer + `opencode run` composition is a fallback only, for anything OpenChamber's scheduler genuinely cannot express.

**Work:**
1. **OpenChamber-scheduled claimant/executor.** An OpenChamber scheduled task on the laptop (any supporting service units defined in the developing-today/code flake — laptop services live there, never in dezren39/nix) that polls the four repo-health queues for tasks whose execution lane is `opencode`, and for each: claims/binds it in the lane ledger **at launch, with the session id recorded** (this closes the launch-binding gap behind the Oct 28 duplicate PRs), launches the session with the route the task packet specifies (Workhorse default; Specialist / Summit for complex work), enforces the 12-session concurrency cap, and records the terminal state (complete / park / block / fail) via the queue helper when the session ends.
2. **Parallel-run gate.** Run beside openchamber-conductor for a defined window (24h or the first 20 executions, whichever is later), comparing bindings and completions. The Muse launch path stands down only after the gate passes.
3. **Stand-down.** Disable the conductor's launch role and retire openchamber-dispatcher and openchamber-babysitter. Muse lanes keep claiming/assigning lanes and verifying results from queue + ledger records.
4. **Supervision.** Scheduling is not supervision (#2019): name how stalled sessions are caught laptop-side (an OpenChamber-scheduled session health check) with Tend's fleet-watchdog reading the ledger as the backstop, and record the choice on this issue.

**Acceptance:**
- A full day with the Muse launch path disabled and opencode-lane completions continuing at or above the pre-change rate.
- 100% of laptop-side launches have a ledger binding with session id at launch time; zero duplicate PRs attributable to unbound launches during the gate.
- Daily check-in reports the opencode lane's per-item cost before/after the change.
- The Muse token cost of the launch path (conductor + predecessors) goes to ~0 for opencode executions.

Routes, pools and the measurement gate are unchanged — this moves *who pulls the trigger*, not what the sessions run on.


## Acceptance criteria
- An OpenChamber scheduled task on the laptop polls the four repo-health queues for opencode-lane tasks, claims/binds each at launch with the session id recorded in the lane ledger, launches it on the packet's route, enforces the 12-session concurrency cap, and records the terminal state via the queue helper.
- The parallel-run gate (24h or the first 20 executions, whichever is later) passes beside openchamber-conductor: 100% of laptop-side launches bound with session id at launch time, zero duplicate PRs attributable to unbound launches.
- After the gate passes, the Muse launch path stands down: openchamber-conductor's launch role disabled, openchamber-dispatcher and openchamber-babysitter retired.
- A full day with the Muse launch path disabled shows opencode-lane completions continuing at or above the pre-change rate, and the Muse token cost of the launch path at ~0 for opencode executions.
- Laptop-side stall supervision is named and recorded on this issue (OpenChamber-scheduled session health check, fleet-watchdog ledger backstop).

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: Additive and reversible only after existing owner/schema review; retain prior data and behavior; no silent fallback or dual authority.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

# DSP-01 — Signed webhook intake and actor authorization boundary

<!-- pmo-9196:DSP-01 -->

**Issue title:** `design(pm-orchestration): Signed webhook intake and actor authorization boundary`  
**Design parent:** #9203 · **Scope:** #9203 direct dispatch/events · **Version:** V3 proposal; not an authorization to implement. **Requirement IDs (ALLOCATED):** C-R005, C-R009, C-R087, C-R088, C-R090, C-R091, C-R107, C-R152, H-R012, H-R016, H-R017, H-R024, H-R031, O-R011, O-R013, O-R014, O-R023, O-R038, O-R047, O-R051, O-R062, O-R074, P-R009, S-R002, S-R004. **Slice status:** curated implementation/research slice. **Pinned baseline:** `a038f084dbeb525494d7bb928ad91f597db2ac51`.

This batch creates design/research/validation handoff issues only. After PR #9225 is merged and this slice's granular prerequisites are resolved, a separately scoped implementation issue may be filed; production adoption, migration, deployment, and live acceptance remain separately authorized stages. The local FDR decisions are accepted design defaults; global #9180 registration is pending and is not a blocker to this bounded design work.

## Goal and deliverable

Reuse existing bounded HMAC webhook intake and authenticated event fanout; add only the missing command authorization/idempotency handoff to canonical Fleet operation intake. Projection delivery dedupe is not accepted-command truth. No duplicate webhook service, database, or projector writeback path.

items.body:
## Gap

The /roadmap page is fed only by a hand-maintained Grist table (doc "Program roadmap", read by sources/live.ts gristRoadmap). The repos' own roadmap records are invisible to the dashboard:

- dezren39/nix has ROADMAP.md (with its Done table, maintained by fleet jobs).
- developing-today/code keeps program roadmaps under planning/roadmaps/ (e.g. planning/roadmaps/id.md is the id program's record) plus .opencode/plans/ phase files.
- The Oct 26 dashboard review found the Grist roadmap held 16 rows with ZERO id rows, while ~68 id issues were open — the hand-kept table drifts from the repo records.

Related but different in scope: code#1216 (add PM stack rows to the code repo's ROADMAP.md / planning files) and code#1352 (program tending). This issue is the dashboard READ side: surface what the repos already record.

## What to build

- A roadmap source in the aggregator that reads the repos' roadmap files from the laptop's primary checkouts (the aggregator already deploys from ~/git/code): ROADMAP.md files and planning/roadmaps/*.md, parsed into RoadmapRow-shaped records (title, area/project, status, horizon when stated, source file + heading anchor as the link).
- Merge with the Grist rows on /roadmap and /api/roadmap.json: each row shows its source (grist vs repo file); repo-derived rows link back to the file/heading.
- Dedup rule: when a Grist row and a repo section describe the same roadmap item (title/area match), prefer the repo row and note the Grist duplicate in provenance rather than showing both.
- Per code#1500's rule, the page must say why a section is empty (file missing vs parse-empty vs source unreadable).

## Acceptance

- /roadmap shows rows derived from at least the code repo's planning/roadmaps/*.md and the nix repo's ROADMAP.md, with source labels and working links.
- The id program appears on the dashboard roadmap from its repo record without any hand entry.
- Grist rows still render; duplicates are collapsed per the rule above; the /api twin matches the page.

Raised by Drew 2026-10-28 ("does roadmap integrate roadmap.md files?" — currently no); companion to the PM event-log issue filed the same day.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] /roadmap and /api/roadmap.json show rows derived from at least the code repo's planning/roadmaps/*.md and the nix repo's ROADMAP.md, with source labels and working links back to the file/heading.
- [ ] The id program appears on the dashboard roadmap from its repo record without any hand entry.
- [ ] Grist rows still render; duplicates are collapsed preferring the repo row with the Grist duplicate noted in provenance; any empty section says why (file missing vs parse-empty vs source unreadable).

items.body:
Phase 3 (closing audit) of design #3068 — "parsed is not validated: one shape contract at every JSON trust boundary" (design doc: `files/designs/code-parsed-is-not-validated.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace). Filed by design-architect pass 26 (2026-10-31); **gated on Phases 1–2 of #3068 landing** (Phase 1: #2938, #2816, #2821, #2974; Phase 2: #2832, #2738, #2800, #2827, #2618). The adopted frame origins of this phase — #2824 and #2802 (id web collab/world frame shape) — are NOT gated on Phases 1–2 and proceed on their own triage; this issue is only the audit + contract statement.

## Scope

Inventory every parse-then-dereference boundary in the surfaces #3068 covers — `bin/`, `scripts/`, `pkgs/` tools (incl. cold-store-reaper and t3code-seed-providers), pm-stack's non-aggregator handlers, and `pkgs/id/web` — i.e. every `JSON.parse`, `response.json()`, `json.loads`, and MessagePack decode whose result is dereferenced. For each hit, disposition it in the closing evidence:

- (a) covered by #3068 Phases 1–3 (name the origin issue), or
- (b) a boundary the phases missed and the same rule covers — fix it under this issue if small and same-rule, otherwise file it as a named follow-up and link it here, or
- (c) not a trust boundary (code-constructed input, or shape already validated at the deref level) — named, with the one-line reason.

## Explicit dispositions required

- **#2608** (cloudflare-export: GraphQL `errors` assumed to be an array of `{message: string}`): decide its ownership once — it sits in a pm-stack exporter that #2576's Phase 3 also touches. Record here (and on #2608) whether it is fixed under #2576's Phase 3 as-built scope or under this design's rule; do not double-file it.
- Every `?? []` / `|| {}` / `?? {}` default at a parse boundary in the inventory: disposition as optional-by-design (the deref site treats absence and emptiness identically on purpose) or absence-as-emptiness (corollary 3 of #3068 — a bug; fix or follow-up per (b)).

## Contract statement

Write the #3068 rule where this repo already states such contracts (bin header docs; the aggregator README's contract section by reference, without reopening #2576's document scope), in the terms the design doc records: validate the shape you deref, at the boundary, before any side effect; exact plain-object vocabulary; failure is the surface's own error; absence is not emptiness; the shared probe matrix (`null`, array, scalar, `{}`, each relied-on field wrong-typed).

items.body:
## Summary

Design #2898 recorded the rule for `pkgs/id` — **reconstruction is admission**: authority-bearing data is validated when created live, so it must be validated where it is rebuilt. Its six origins were the journal seams known that evening. Four more instances have since been filed, in three shapes its phases did not cover — two of them in state that did not exist when #2898 was written:

- **#3942** — checkpoint-carried handoff state is installed, not validated. The region-seam transfers added by #3870 phase 1 (PR #3922) are checked strictly as standalone `EntityExported`/`EntityImported` entries (`core.rs:322-375`), but a `Checkpoint`'s `transfers` list is assigned verbatim (`core.handoff_transfers = transfers.unwrap_or_default()`, `core.rs:504`): duplicate `(handoff_id, direction)` sides, a non-advancing import epoch, and a sequence-claiming transfer event all restore `Ok` (laptop probe against the real `restore`), while the same arm validates the profile, the caps ceiling, and schedule agreement for everything else it carries. Compaction launders bad transfer state into the canonical durable form.
- **#3736 + #3961** — restore's own succession checks use a plain `+ 1`, the only two admission predicates in `core.rs` that do (every sibling uses `checked_add`/`saturating_add`). Checkpoint event consecutiveness (`core.rs:476`) accepts a wrapped `u64::MAX → 0` step in release and panics in debug; the `EntityImported` epoch advance (`core.rs:368`) accepts `prior = u64::MAX, new = 0` in release — the fencing epoch going backwards — and panics in debug.
- **#3911** — `WaitingPool::restore` (id-core `waiting.rs:312`) checks only already-held; `insert` and `park` both also refuse arrived and ready-queue keys (the guard set closed #2001 established). The event store routes every hold through `restore`, so an already-applied event can be held and handed out a second time. One caller (the fork-proof park) relies on the gap on purpose — see decision 3.

#2898's closing-audit scope (sandbox snapshot, `restore_program`, petname persistence) names none of these surfaces; the transfers field did not exist then. This design is #2898's follow-on — the same pattern as #2497 following #1554 — and re-scopes none of its phases.

Full design doc: `files/designs/code-id-restore-admission-followon.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Audit baseline: origin/main `83709fac` (all sites below read verbatim at HEAD this pass).

## The contract

> **Every path into state is admission.** State that arrives carried inside a reconstruction container is validated item-by-item with exactly the rules its standalone form is validated with, before it is installed. A succession predicate in an admission path is checked arithmetic: the successor of `u64::MAX` does not exist, so the entry is refused — never wrapped to 0, never a panic. And a reconstruction entry point applies the same guard set as the live entry points of the same structure; any deliberate relaxation is a named, separate route, not a silent property of the restore path.

## Recorded decisions

1. **Carried transfers are validated by the standalone rules, with the standalone errors** — per element, in list order, before assignment: no duplicate `(handoff_id, direction)`; an import's `new_owner_epoch` is the checked successor of `prior_owner_epoch`; an export carries no `new_owner_epoch` (#3942's acceptance); each transfer's `event` has `sequence == 0 && participant_id == 0`. Refusal aborts the whole restore. One shared per-transfer validation helper is preferred so the arms cannot drift a third time, but the contract is the equivalence, not the refactor. Replaying transfers through the standalone arms loses (the arms push replay events and bump counters; checkpoint transfers are already-applied state).
2. **Succession is `checked_add`, not `saturating_add`.** Saturation would let `MAX → MAX` pass an advance check; it is the right idiom for counters that may sit at a cap (`since_checkpoint`) and the wrong one for a predicate whose job is that the value moved. The two filed sites are the whole `core.rs` inventory (grep-verified this pass); the closing audit greps the rest of `pkgs/id`.
3. **The waiting pool's guards are the pool's guards — with the proof park made explicit.** `restore` gains the ready-queue guard unconditionally and the arrived guard on its hold path. The deliberate exception — `present_proof` re-holding an arrived fork-proof header for good so its conflicts stay seen — becomes an explicit held-for-good route (a `park`-style entry), not a borrowed missing guard. Copying `insert`'s guard verbatim without moving the proof caller loses: it silently un-parks proof headers. `restore`'s capacity posture (larger-cap stores still open; excess drops, never wedges) is unchanged.
4. **No wire-format or writer change.** Live writers cannot produce any refused state — standalone validation is what they already pass, and #3942's controls show a valid checkpoint restores `Ok` — so restore strictness is safe for every journal live code can write (#2898's original strictness argument).

Alternatives that lose (in the doc): folding these into #2898's Phase 3 audit (a named bounded scope inside #2882/#2876; stretching it re-scopes their acceptance from a comment); a Phase 1 bound on the transfers list (no cap value is recorded anywhere — the closing audit dispositions it instead).

## Phased breakdown

- **Phase 1 — checkpoint-carried handoffs are validated (adopted: #3942).** Per its acceptance. Lands first: the trust-boundary hole, and #3870's coordinator phases 2–5 assume the dedupe/epoch invariants it protects.
- **Phase 2 — succession is checked arithmetic (adopted: #3736 + #3961).** Both predicates become checked-successor comparisons; `u64::MAX` boundary tests at each site (refusal must be restore's own error in both build profiles); same-file grep proof. Independent of Phase 1 in code — but Phase 1's carried-import epoch check uses the checked form, so whichever lands second writes that predicate in its final shape exactly once.
- **Phase 3a — the waiting pool's restore applies the pool's guards (adopted: #3911).** Per its acceptance and decision 3 (explicit proof-park route, behaviour pinned by test). Independent of Phases 1–2 (different crate).
- **Phase 3b — closing audit (new issue, gated on Phases 1, 2 and 3a).** Reconstruction-entry-point inventory for `pkgs/id` with a disposition per surface (citing #2898 Phase 3's outcomes where scopes overlap rather than re-auditing); a crate-wide grep disposition for plain arithmetic inside admission predicates; the transfers-bound disposition; a cross-note on #2898.

Open questions stay in the design doc (a bound on active handoffs — no recorded value, dispositioned by Phase 3b; snapshot-content equivalence — #2898 Phase 3's scope, cited not duplicated; store-row cleanup for arrived/ready refusals on reload — Phase 3a triage records it).

Related: #2898 (parent design — a follow-on note is posted there), #3870 (its phases 2–5 are untouched implementation work), #3231 (same crate, different gate — artifact `parsed()`, no field overlap). Not this design: #3963/#3964 (BoardGraph live-construction checks, no reconstruction surface); #2882's schedule arithmetic (a live-path check, stays in #2898's scope — Phase 2 here is restore succession predicates only).

🤖 Design architect pass 34 (2026-11-01), audit at origin/main `83709fac`.
